Their statics teach '14% elemental' and 'sludge means buffered': be ready to answer with the lab report.
Best idea for SILT: a two-week 'ask your own tracker' test with real customers' screenshots, aimed at desk workers.

teardowns.summary: The Beckham-backed all-in-one drink. Meta lists 42,281 US ads; this is a sample of 1,009, mostly May to October and 940 of them stopped, so it shows their past playbook, not today.
highlights: They borrow trust: Beckham is named in 357 ads but on screen in only 1 of the top 15. Doctors, one trial number and athlete shareholders do the selling.
One of their longest statics (80 days, 69 versions) sells a day and night pair, the same logic as Mornings + Nights.
Their newest angle is SILT territory: every dose on the label, no proprietary blend, glycinate not oxide.
Best idea for SILT: founder to camera, "Skeptical of supplements? Good. Here is every report.", opening each lab report.
